## Creation of annotation information
There is no official org.db package for honey bees so we need to create our own annotation information.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(clusterProfiler)
```

## Setup

Setup the supporting information needed

```{r}
options(timeout = 3600)

taxid <- "7460"
dir.create("annotation", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Read a large gzipped NCBI table in chunks and keep only the honey bee rows
# (base R only, works on Windows/macOS/Linux)
filter_ncbi <- function(url, dest, taxid) {
  if (!file.exists(dest)) download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb")
  con <- gzfile(dest, "r"); on.exit(close(con))
  pat  <- paste0("^", taxid, "\t")
  keep <- character(0)
  repeat {
    chunk <- readLines(con, n = 500000)
    if (length(chunk) == 0) break
    keep <- c(keep, grep(pat, chunk, value = TRUE))
  }
  read.delim(text = keep, header = FALSE, sep = "\t", quote = "",
             comment.char = "", fill = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

```

## Add NCBI GENE IDs
We need the NCBI GENE IDs to select the enrchichment terms.

```{r}
gi <- filter_ncbi(
  "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/DATA/GENE_INFO/Invertebrates/All_Invertebrates.gene_info.gz",
  "annotation/All_Invertebrates.gene_info.gz", taxid)
gene_map <- data.frame(GeneID = as.character(gi$V2), Symbol = gi$V3,
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
message("Honey bee genes in NCBI gene_info: ", nrow(gene_map))

```

## Select the GO terms
now we can select the GO terms involved with apis mellifera, and save the annotation information for further analysis
```{r}
g2go <- filter_ncbi("https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/DATA/gene2go.gz",
                    "annotation/gene2go.gz", taxid)
g2go <- g2go[!grepl("^NOT", g2go$V5), ]                    # drop negated annotations
go   <- unique(data.frame(GeneID = as.character(g2go$V2), GO = g2go$V3,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
go   <- merge(go, gene_map, by = "GeneID")
write.table(unique(go[, c("Symbol", "GO")]), "annotation_terms/gene2go.tsv", sep = "\t",
            quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
message("GO: ", length(unique(go$Symbol)), " genes, ",
        length(unique(go$GO)), " GO terms")
```

## Select the KEGG terms
We can do the same now for the KEGG pathways
```{r}
kk  <- download_KEGG("ame")
p2g <- kk$KEGGPATHID2EXTID; colnames(p2g) <- c("path", "GeneID")
p2n <- kk$KEGGPATHID2NAME;  colnames(p2n) <- c("path", "name")
p2n$name  <- sub(" - Apis mellifera.*$", "", p2n$name)
p2g$GeneID <- as.character(p2g$GeneID)
kegg <- merge(merge(p2g, p2n, by = "path"), gene_map, by = "GeneID")
write.table(unique(kegg[, c("Symbol", "path", "name")]), "annotation_terms/gene2kegg.tsv",
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
message("KEGG: ", length(unique(kegg$Symbol)), " genes, ",
        length(unique(kegg$path)), " pathways")
```


## Check the coverage
Check the coverage of the found terms so we can see how many genes have terms related to them
```{r}
ids <- rownames(read.csv(file.path(getwd(),"gene_counts_matrix.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
message(sprintf("Your genes with GO annotation:   %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                sum(ids %in% go$Symbol), length(ids), 100 * mean(ids %in% go$Symbol)))
message(sprintf("Your genes with KEGG annotation: %d / %d (%.1f%%)",
                sum(ids %in% kegg$Symbol), length(ids), 100 * mean(ids %in% kegg$Symbol)))
